messages:
mike: CI image publish is flapping on the push step for build #2582 — pushing to our private registry returns 401 on some chunk uploads. Happens ~1/3 runs. Logs below. Anyone seen this pattern recently?

mike: ```
INFO: Pushing layer 3/10
ERROR: unexpected status: 401 Unauthorized (upload chunk 3/10)
retrying...
INFO: pushing manifest
ERROR: push failed: manifest upload returned 401
```

deploy-bot: publish-job-2582 started by mike (ci) :white_check_mark:

sophie: ugh. did we rotate registry creds recently?

mike: Not intentionally. Anna did a k8s secret rotate last week but that was for cluster infra, not the registry.

anna: I rotated a subset of service keys for the helm deployers on Monday — not the push token the CI uses. I can double-check though. Which token is the job using?

mike: It uses CI_REGISTRY_TOKEN from the shared secrets mounted into the runners (ops-jenkins secret).

jordan: Could be sourcery: I've seen blob/chunked uploads hit 401 when the token had a short TTL and the upload takes > TTL (kaniko does multi-chunk uploads). Any chance the token got issued with short expiry?

mike: Good call. The token TTL is normally 2h. Build takes ~12m so should be fine. But this is intermittent.

sophie: Another possibility: parallel chunk uploads + manifest race on the registry side. Harbor had a bug where concurrent chunk commits occasionally returned 401 if a GC was running. We had a similar incident months ago.

mike: I can repro locally by re-running the job in debug mode. Will try kaniko with --single-snapshot and --debug to see chunk timing.

anna: If you can reproduce, try pushing with docker push (single stream) vs kaniko to compare. Also check registry logs around the 401 timestamps (harbor-core / nginx).

mike: Repro attempt: ran kaniko debug locally, forced parallelism (default). Got 401 on chunk 5/10. Pasted kaniko log:

mike: ```
I0301 14:12:05.123] Uploading chunk 5/10 to https://registry.internal/v2/blobs/uploads/...
I0301 14:12:06.987] server response: 401 Unauthorized
I0301 14:12:06.987] response headers: 
  Www-Authenticate: Bearer realm=..., error="invalid_token"
```

jordan: That header suggests the registry thinks the token is invalid/expired at that moment. Maybe a clock skew on the registry auth server?

anna: We had a small NTP drift on a node last week but fixed it. Will check auth server logs for token validation failures matching those timestamps.

ops-jenkins: Re-triggered job #2582 rerun-1 (mike) :arrow_forward:

sophie: In the meantime, try setting kaniko flag --single-snapshot or --no-parallel-upload to see if serial uploads avoid the 401. If that stabilizes, it's likely a race/registry-side issue.

mike: Rerun logs (rerun-1): push succeeded. So the rerun was green.

mike: Ran a few more reruns. 2/5 failed with 401, 3/5 succeeded. Changing to --no-parallel-upload for a build fixed it locally (no 401).

jordan: OK that strongly points at concurrent chunk handling in the registry or a transient auth service hiccup under parallel requests.

anna: I pulled auth logs: a handful of "invalid_token" checks for our CI client at 14:12:06 — token lookup returned null for a very short window while a cache refresh happened. Could be our memcached cluster briefly returned 500.

mike: Can ops add resiliency? e.g., retry logic on 401 for chunk uploads, or make kaniko use serialized uploads by default until the registry is patched.

ops-jenkins: We can add an env var override for kaniko args in the pipeline template (CI_KANIKO_OPTS). I'll open a quick MR to default to --no-parallel-upload for the registry repo group.

sophie: Also add a short exponential backoff retry for 401 errors in the push step (3 retries) — that helps with transient auth cache issues.

anna: On infra side I'll open a ticket for the registry team to investigate memcached flaps and add metrics/alerts. Will include correlation with GC windows and auth cache refreshes.

mike: Thanks. I pushed a small pipeline MR that: 1) sets CI_KANIKO_OPTS="--no-parallel-upload" for the repo group, 2) retries push step up to 3x on 401.

mike: MR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ci/pipelines/-/merge_requests/342 — feel free to review.

sophie: Reviewed and approved :thumbsup: We'll roll this to canary first.

deploy-bot: pipeline MR-342 merged by sophie at 14:55 UTC

anna: Infra ticket: RG-1979 tracking memcached auth cache blips + registry chunked upload 401s. I'm assigning to registry SRE.

mike: Great. Marking this thread resolved for now — will reopen if we see failures after the pipeline change and registry fix. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
